statement.document_title: Three years on, ChatGPT still isn't what it was cracked up to be – and it probably never will be

from_speaker: auto-generated code tends to be shaky
few amateurs can make those prototypes robust
our_interpretation: Amateurs means people without substantial software-development expertise.
Shaky means recurring functional, security, or maintenance defects beyond a successful demonstration.
Robust means reliable operation under realistic use, including testing, error handling, security, and maintenance.
Few means a small minority; Marcus supplies no numerical cutoff.
For this ongoing observation, I use July–September 2025, the latest completed calendar quarter before publication. The quarter is an evaluator convention, not a period stated by Marcus.
criteria.support_condition: Relevant studies show that amateurs can create working prototypes, that defects commonly remain, and that only a small minority can independently bring comparable prototypes to robust operation.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evidence shows that amateurs commonly produce and independently harden comparable applications to robust operation, or that the claimed recurring defects are uncommon.

evidence.explanation: The review synthesizes 101 practitioner sources and reports a speed–quality trade-off. Its mixed population, self-selected accounts, and insufficiently precise observation dates prevent treating it as a quarter-specific measurement of how few amateurs can harden applications.

The report describes functional demonstrations and quality problems among 31 participants in nine teams. It does not establish the event within the target quarter or measure subsequent production-hardening success; the authors expressly decline generalizability.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A representative study of amateurs using tools available during the target period, with independent application testing and follow-up measuring how many successfully harden their prototypes.
